items.followUp: How does atomic size change across a period and down a group?

rubric.why: Tests the periodic trend across a period.
rubric.description: Electropositivity decreases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the direction and decrease across a period.

rubric.why: Tests the periodic trend down a group.
rubric.description: Electropositivity increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the increase down a group.

modelAnswer: Across a period, electropositivity decreases from left to right.
Down a group, electropositivity increases.

items.followUp: State how electronegativity changes across a period and down a group.

rubric.why: Identifies the permitted orbits and their fixed energies.
rubric.description: Electrons revolve in certain permitted orbits, each with a definite energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons occupy permitted orbits with fixed energy.

rubric.why: States that an electron's energy remains unchanged while it stays in an orbit.
rubric.description: An electron does not radiate or lose energy while revolving in a permitted orbit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons do not radiate energy in a permitted orbit.

rubric.why: Recognises that energy exchange occurs during transitions between orbits.
rubric.description: An electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps from one orbit to another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking absorption or emission of energy with an orbit transition.

rubric.why: States what determines the energy absorbed or emitted.
rubric.description: The absorbed or emitted energy equals the difference between the energies of the two orbits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the energy change equals the difference between orbit energies.

rubric.why: Includes the standard relation for the energy of the transition.
rubric.description: The energy change is given by ΔE = E₂ − E₁ = hν.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the relation ΔE = E₂ − E₁ = hν, or its equivalent in words.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain permitted orbits, each having a definite energy.
An electron does not radiate or lose energy while it remains in a permitted orbit.
An electron absorbs or emits energy only when it jumps from one orbit to another.
The energy absorbed or emitted equals the difference between the energies of the two orbits.
This energy change is given by ΔE = E₂ − E₁ = hν.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an atom and a monatomic ion, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Defines a molecule by its neutral state and bonded atoms.
rubric.description: A molecule is a neutral group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a molecule as a neutral bonded group of atoms.

rubric.why: Checks that the student can identify a molecule.
rubric.description: A suitable example of a molecule is H₂O, O₂, N₂ or CO₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct molecule example.

rubric.why: Defines a molecular ion by its net charge.
rubric.description: A molecular ion is a group of covalently bonded atoms carrying a net charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a molecular ion as a bonded group of atoms with a charge.

rubric.why: Checks that the student can identify a molecular ion.
rubric.description: A suitable example is NH₄⁺, SO₄²⁻, NO₃⁻ or CO₃²⁻.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct molecular-ion example.

modelAnswer: A molecule is a neutral group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together; for example, H₂O.
A molecular ion is a group of covalently bonded atoms carrying a net charge; for example, NH₄⁺.

items.followUp: What are covalent compounds? State four of their properties.

rubric.why: Checks the defining ionic attraction in these compounds.
rubric.description: Ionic compounds consist of oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining ionic compounds in terms of oppositely charged ions and their attraction.

rubric.why: Identifies the characteristic solid structure.
rubric.description: They are crystalline solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionic compounds are crystalline solids.

rubric.why: Identifies their high melting or boiling points.
rubric.description: They generally have high melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they have high melting or boiling points.

rubric.why: Identifies their usual solubility behaviour.
rubric.description: They are generally soluble in water or other polar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionic compounds are generally soluble in water or polar solvents.

rubric.why: Identifies electrical conduction when ions can move.
rubric.description: They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not as solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they conduct electricity in molten or aqueous solution.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are compounds made of oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.
They are crystalline solids.
They generally have high melting and boiling points.
They are generally soluble in water or other polar solvents.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state.

items.followUp: Describe four factors that affect the rate of diffusion of gases.

rubric.why: Temperature affects the motion of liquid particles and thus their diffusion rate.
rubric.description: Increasing temperature increases the rate of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the effect of temperature.

rubric.why: A stronger concentration difference drives faster net diffusion.
rubric.description: A greater concentration gradient increases the rate of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the effect of concentration difference or gradient.

rubric.why: Particle size influences how readily particles move through the liquid.
rubric.description: Smaller particles diffuse faster than larger particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the effect of particle or molecular size.

rubric.why: The medium's resistance to particle movement affects diffusion.
rubric.description: Diffusion is faster in a less viscous or less dense liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the effect of liquid viscosity or density.

modelAnswer: Higher temperature increases the rate of diffusion because liquid particles move faster.
A greater concentration gradient increases the rate of diffusion.
Smaller particles diffuse faster than larger particles.
Diffusion is faster in a less viscous, less dense liquid because it offers less resistance to particle movement.

items.followUp: Define solubility and explain why some solutes dissolve in some solvents but not others.

rubric.why: Checks that solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves.
rubric.description: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the maximum amount of solute that dissolves.

rubric.why: Solubility is specified for a saturated solution at a particular temperature.
rubric.description: The amount is stated for a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including saturation and the temperature condition.

rubric.why: States the general principle governing solubility.
rubric.description: The general principle of solubility is “like dissolves like.”
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the principle.

rubric.why: Explains the principle through the matching nature of solute and solvent.
rubric.description: Polar solutes tend to dissolve in polar solvents, and non-polar solutes in non-polar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that substances with similar polarity dissolve one another.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
The general principle is “like dissolves like.”
Thus, polar solutes tend to dissolve in polar solvents, while non-polar solutes tend to dissolve in non-polar solvents.

rubric.why: Checks both that biochemistry is a branch of chemistry and that it concerns living organisms.
rubric.description: Biochemistry is the branch of chemistry concerned with chemical substances and reactions in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a branch of chemistry and 1 mark for stating that it deals with substances or reactions in living organisms.

modelAnswer: Biochemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with the chemical substances and reactions occurring in living organisms.

items.followUp: Define a molecular formula and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition explains what information a chemical formula represents.
rubric.description: A chemical formula uses symbols and numbers to show the kinds and numbers of atoms or ions in a substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the information represented by a chemical formula.

rubric.why: Checks for a valid example of a chemical formula.
rubric.description: A correct example is H₂O, NaCl, CO₂ or NH₃.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a valid chemical formula as an example.

modelAnswer: A chemical formula is a shorthand representation using symbols and numbers to show the kinds and numbers of atoms or ions in a substance.
For example, H₂O represents water.
